name: Read an Invoice
description: Business Ladder, Finance & Accounts, Level 1 (Assist). One supplier invoice per case, copied from a PDF: fill in the accounts-system form (supplier, invoice number, dates, net/VAT/gross, VAT number, PO reference, whether the bank details have changed, and the account to pay). Later cases add the traps real invoices have: our own VAT number next to the supplier’s, a delivery-note number that looks like the invoice number, an earlier balance added to the amount due, a US-format date flagged as such, an OCR scan that reads 0 as O, and an amendment that changes a line so the totals must be recalculated.
hook: One invoice, twelve boxes to fill. Can it read the paperwork without slipping?
author: Gauntlet Core

cases.prompt:
I work in accounts payable at Larkspur Events Ltd. Here is a supplier invoice that has just arrived (text copied from the PDF). Please read it and fill in the form for our accounts system.

Invoice:
<<<
NORTHGATE SUPPLIES LTD
Unit 22, Canal Street, Sheffield S3 8EN
VAT Reg No: GB 820 3958 34    Company No: 29866475

TAX INVOICE

Invoice No: INV-36677        Invoice Date: 09/02/2026
Your Order Ref: PO-93282

Invoice to: Larkspur Events Ltd, Unit 15, Victoria Way, Cardiff CF10 4LJ
FAO: Grace Kowalski, Accounts Payable

Qty | Description | Unit price | VAT | Net
11 | A4 copier paper 80gsm (box of 5 reams) | £21.50 | 20% | £236.50
18 | Nitrile gloves, blue, medium (box of 100) | £6.99 | 20% | £125.82

Net total: £362.32
VAT: £72.46
Invoice total: £434.78

Payment due by 9 March 2026.
Please pay by BACS to Northgate Supplies Ltd, sort code 45-90-36, account 75581965, quoting the invoice number.
Queries: grace@northgate.example.co.uk
>>>

Form (reply with this JSON object, filled in):
{
  "supplier": string,               // the supplier company name exactly as it is registered (e.g. "Acme Widgets Ltd")
  "invoice_number": string,         // the supplier’s invoice number, e.g. "INV-12345"
  "invoice_date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
  "due_date": "YYYY-MM-DD",         // as stated, or worked out from the payment terms
  "net": number,                    // amount before VAT, in pounds
  "vat": number,                    // VAT, in pounds
  "gross": number,                  // total of THIS invoice including VAT, in pounds
  "supplier_vat_number": string,    // e.g. "GB123456789"
  "po_reference": string or null,   // OUR purchase order number quoted on the invoice; null if none is quoted
  "bank_details_changed": true or false,  // does the invoice say the supplier’s bank details have changed?
  "sort_code": "NN-NN-NN",          // the account the invoice tells us to pay into now
  "account_number": string
}

Rules:
- Dates on UK documents are day/month/year unless the document says otherwise.
- Due dates: "N days from the invoice date" means the invoice date plus N calendar days. "End of the month following" means the last day of the next calendar month.
- If the invoice states an amendment, use the amended figures: recalculate net, VAT (20% on standard-rated lines, 0% on zero-rated lines; delivery is standard-rated) and gross yourself, rounding VAT to the nearest penny.
- gross is the total of this invoice only: do not add any earlier balance.
- Reply with ONE JSON object (a ```json block is fine) and nothing else after it. Numbers as plain JSON numbers. Give exactly one value per field: a field holding two values, a range or an "X or Y" answer is marked wrong. Every field is checked separately.
cases.notes: features: lines=2, terms=date; printed totals net 362.32 vat 72.46 gross 434.78
